summary: This is a JUnit test that checks what a Thermostat prints to the screen. Because printStatusToDisplay() writes to System.out instead of returning a value, the test temporarily redirects System.out into a buffer, calls the method, and then compares the captured text against the expected message.

lines.text: A ByteArrayOutputStream collects bytes in memory rather than sending them anywhere, which makes it a convenient place to catch printed output.
System.out is a PrintStream, so the test needs this class to build a replacement one.
A static import lets the test call assertEquals directly instead of writing Assertions.assertEquals every time.
This placeholder stands for the tests written earlier in the chapter; only the new one is printed here to keep the listing short.
This annotation marks the method as a test case so JUnit finds and runs it automatically.
The thermostat starts at 72 degrees with heating off, which is the exact state that should report "Idle".
Saving the real System.out first is essential, because the test must put it back afterwards or every later test would lose its output.
From this point on, anything printed goes into the in-memory buffer instead of the console.
This is the method under test, and its printed text lands in the buffer.
A finally block runs even if the method throws an exception, guaranteeing the cleanup below always happens.
Restoring the original stream leaves the test environment exactly as it was found.
The expected value includes System.lineSeparator() because println adds a newline, and using the platform separator keeps the test passing on Windows as well as Linux and macOS.
